# griddy

`griddy` is an R package for geospatial distribution dynamics with `sf`
and tidy data. It is inspired by PySAL `giddy` and by established
spatial distribution dynamics work, especially Rey (2001). Prior R
implementations exist, including `estdaR` and `spdyn`, but neither is on
CRAN or designed along tidy principles. This package is designed to work
best with long data and `sf` native spatial workflows.

Current scope:

- classify longitudinal spatial values into comparable classes
- estimate classic Markov transition matrices
- estimate spatial Markov transition matrices conditioned on spatial lag
  class
- compute simple rank mobility
- summarize sojourn times, first-passage times, and scalar Markov
  mobility
- test whether transition dynamics differ across regimes
- return tidy tables and `ggplot2` plots

Version 0.2.0 extends the core workflow with chain summaries and
inferential tests for transition-regime homogeneity.

## Installation

``` r
# CRAN release
install.packages("griddy")

# Development version
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("dshkol/griddy")
```

The minimal example below also uses `spData` for state geometry:

``` r
install.packages("spData")
```

## What it does

`griddy` keeps the workflow keyed by explicit `id`, `time`, and `value`
columns instead of matrix row position. The analytical outputs preserve
transition labels, class intervals, and spatial-lag intervals so they
can be inspected, joined, and plotted without reverse-engineering array
dimensions.

## Minimal example

The bundled `usjoin` panel is the canonical PySAL `giddy` reference
dataset: 48 contiguous US states, per-capita personal income, 1929 to
2009.

``` r
library(griddy)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(sfdep)
library(spData)

data(usjoin)

geom <- us_states |>
  filter(NAME %in% usjoin$name) |>
  mutate(
    nb = st_contiguity(geometry),
    wt = st_weights(nb)
  )

panel <- usjoin |>
  filter(name %in% geom$NAME) |>
  arrange(name, year)

classes <- classify_dynamics(panel, name, year, income, k = 5)
classic <- markov_dynamics(classes, name, year, class)
spatial <- spatial_markov(
  panel, name, year, income,
  geometry = geom, geometry_id = NAME, k = 5
)

classic$transitions |> select(id, from_time, to_time, transition) |> head()
lag_intervals(spatial)
```

[`spatial_markov()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/spatial_markov.md)
takes a `geometry` argument: an `sf` tibble with one row per spatial
unit and `nb` / `wt` list-columns produced by `sfdep`. This keeps the
spatial frame, neighbor structure, and row-standardization choice in one
tidy object. Rows of `geometry` are matched to panel units by id,
through the column named in `geometry_id` or a column with the same name
as `id`. `listw` and `nb` arguments remain accepted for compatibility
with existing workflows.

## Documentation

The pkgdown site is organized around:

- core workflow and concepts, including chain summaries and homogeneity
  tests
- `tidycensus` and `cancensus` examples showing applications with US and
  Canadian census data
- coverage of PySAL `giddy`: what `griddy` implements, short recipes for
  the rest, and what is planned
- prior-art comparison against `estdaR` and `spdyn`
- performance benchmarking notes
- a usage guide for LLMs and coding agents, with an
  [`llms.txt`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/llms.txt) index of the
  site

AI coding agents contributing to `griddy` should start with
[`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/dshkol/griddy/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

# Package index

## Core Workflow

- [`classify_dynamics()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/classify_dynamics.md)
  : Classify Longitudinal Values For Distribution Dynamics
- [`class_intervals()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/class_intervals.md)
  : Class Intervals Used By A griddy Object
- [`markov_dynamics()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/markov_dynamics.md)
  : Estimate Classic Markov Transition Dynamics
- [`transition_matrix()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/transition_matrix.md)
  : Extract A Transition Matrix
- [`steady_state()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/steady_state.md)
  : Estimate Stationary Distribution
- [`spatial_markov()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/spatial_markov.md)
  : Estimate Spatial Markov Transition Dynamics
- [`lag_intervals()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/lag_intervals.md)
  : Spatial Lag Intervals Used By A Spatial Markov Object
- [`rank_mobility()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/rank_mobility.md)
  : Compute Rank Mobility

## Chain Summaries

- [`sojourn_time()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/sojourn_time.md)
  : Expected Sojourn Times
- [`first_passage()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/first_passage.md)
  : Mean First-Passage Times
- [`mobility_index()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/mobility_index.md)
  : Markov Mobility Indices

## Inference

- [`homogeneity_test()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/homogeneity_test.md)
  : Test Homogeneity Of Transition Matrices Across Regimes

## Plotting

- [`plot_transition_matrix()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/plot_transition_matrix.md)
  : Plot A Transition Matrix
- [`plot_spatial_markov()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/plot_spatial_markov.md)
  : Plot Spatial Markov Matrices
- [`plot_rank_mobility()`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/plot_rank_mobility.md)
  : Plot Rank Mobility

## Data

- [`usjoin`](https://dshkol.github.io/griddy/reference/usjoin.md) : US
  State Per-Capita Personal Income, 1929-2009
